title: Starting age, father's cornet and the Tosseau nickname
summary: He started around 16, had borrowed his father's cornet earlier, was nicknamed after bandleader Emile Tosseau, and taught himself by ear.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: How old were you when you started?
I was about 16. About 16. First, I started when I was a kid around, well, when I got the plaintiff's job, yeah. Yeah.
But before then, I was around nine, ten years old. Did you start right on the car net?
Yeah, that's all, a little brass corner. Did you pick up your father sometime and use it?
I caught him for doing it, see? Yeah, I bet. Oh, Jesus. I put a dent in it one day, oh, Jesus.
What was your father's name, by the way? Edward. Edward.
Edward. Edward Lopez. And he was quite well known down there, amongst the old timers in those days.

Armand Vesey, Emile Tosseau. So, when I was going to get to the, the Wood Crab Boys had a parade or something one day. And here I am up the line, blowing on my bugle, see? Yeah. And the kids all nicknamed me Tosseau. Tosseau used to have the band out of the Spanish Forge. Oh, that's right, I've heard of that.

He led the offing for 20, 25 years. So, the nickname me Tosseau, there, see? There he went. Well, Tosseau, he's the last guy I saw with it, one of those things, you know? So, I was Tosseau all the way. So, then, from there on, I got picking up little pieces here and there. Never had no idea what to play with anybody, but just for myself, see?
Had you played on anything else first, like a guitar or drums or anything when you were a kid, or a tin whistle or anything like that? No.

Oh, I had a tin whistle. I could play that however, one of them tin whistles. Oh, yeah. But, it just comes natural to me, you know? Yeah. Nobody showed me the scale, you had to fork a couple of notes, you know? Yeah. But, it just came, I practiced, I wasn't right off the bat, but I... Yeah, sure. Then I got to say, my mother said, take that.
